business_problem: Hunliji's wedding-services platform had outgrown a self-built data warehouse. The company needed to process hundreds of millions of behavioral events per day, manage large image assets, and support marketing, order, risk-control, and payment workloads, but its earlier stack suffered from unclear lineage, inconsistent metrics, unstable scheduling, and too little automation for multi-engine data development. It also wanted an AI-assisted way to generate and optimize SQL, manage complex workflows, and improve developer productivity across a growing lakehouse estate.
solution_summary: Hunliji rebuilt its data estate on Alibaba Cloud around DataWorks so operational analytics and AI-assisted development could run on one governed lakehouse platform. Logs and business data are integrated through DataWorks into an OSS-HDFS data lake, where offline pipelines use Spark and Hive for layered warehouse processing while real-time streams land in Paimon through Flink. Trino and Doris provide interactive analysis for downstream users, and the new Data Studio plus workflow capabilities orchestrate multi-engine jobs, Python tasks, and lineage-aware scheduling from one control plane. The AI layer comes from DataWorks Copilot, which lets engineers generate, correct, optimize, and translate SQL or UDF logic with natural-language interaction, and also supports table discovery, table creation, and engine-parameter guidance. The result is a governed Data+AI environment that supports marketing analytics, user insight, risk monitoring, and merchant operations at production scale.

solution_components.name: DataWorks
solution_components.role: Provides the central development, scheduling, modeling, governance, and workflow control plane for Hunliji's enterprise data platform.

solution_components.name: OSS-HDFS data lake
solution_components.role: Stores integrated log and business data for downstream offline and real-time lakehouse processing.

solution_components.name: Spark
solution_components.role: Runs offline transformation and layered processing jobs over large-scale platform data.

solution_components.name: Hive
solution_components.role: Supports warehouse-style offline processing on top of the governed data model.

solution_components.name: Flink
solution_components.role: Streams real-time data into the lakehouse so fresh operational data can be analyzed continuously.

solution_components.name: Paimon
solution_components.role: Acts as the real-time lakehouse table format for streaming data landed by Flink.

solution_components.name: Trino
solution_components.role: Provides interactive analytics over processed data for business and engineering teams.

solution_components.name: Doris
solution_components.role: Serves processed analytical outputs for downstream decision support and operational reporting.

solution_components.name: DataWorks Copilot
solution_components.role: Uses natural-language interaction to generate, optimize, convert, and troubleshoot data-development logic for engineers.

data_flow: Hunliji integrates log and business data through DataWorks into an OSS-HDFS data lake, processes offline layers with Spark and Hive, and streams real-time events through Flink into Paimon tables. Trino and Doris expose processed datasets for analysis and reporting, while DataWorks workflows orchestrate the jobs and DataWorks Copilot helps engineers generate SQL, convert code, and resolve development issues across the same governed environment.
business_outcome: Hunliji moved from a brittle self-built warehouse to a governed lakehouse platform that can support high-volume wedding-industry data operations and AI-assisted engineering from one environment. The redesign gave the team clearer lineage, more flexible Python and workflow execution, faster multi-engine development, and a practical Copilot layer for SQL generation, optimization, and diagnostics. That lets the platform keep supporting user insight, advertising, merchant service, and risk-control scenarios at growing scale.
